Mount Kilauea, located on the Big Island of Hawaii, erupted for the 43rd time in its current eruptive cycle, sending up lava fountains and triggering a rare Ashfall Warning for surrounding areas.

Ashfall warnings are uncommon even during active volcanic periods and indicate that ash and debris are being carried by wind in amounts that could affect communities near the volcano.
